facts.statement: The genus Metopacanthus was first described by Zittel in 1887.
Metopacanthus granulatus is the type species of the genus Metopacanthus.
Metopacanthus belongs to the family Myriacanthidae.
Metopacanthus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Metopacanthus was an extinct genus of holocephalan cartilaginous fish that lived in Europe during the Early Jurassic epoch.
facts.quote: Metopacanthus is an extinct genus of holocephalan cartilaginous fish from the Early Jurassic epoch in Europe.

facts.statement: Fossils of Metopacanthus are found in the Toarcian stage of the Posidonia Shale in Germany.
facts.quote: It is known from the Toarcian of the Posidonia Shale of Germany.

facts.statement: Metopacanthus possessed an unusual jaw-like structure located over its skull.
facts.quote: It has an unusual jaw-like structure over the skull.

facts.statement: Metopacanthus had a long fin spine measuring 33 cm in length.
facts.quote: It had long fin spine with length of 33 cm.

facts.statement: Metopacanthus lived between the Sinemurian and Toarcian stages, from 199.5 to 182.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Toarcian (199.5 to 182.9 million years ago)
